woodSpecies.name: Hard Sugar Maple (Acer saccharum)
woodSpecies.naturalAntimicrobialProperties: Moderate (Natural capillary desiccation; draws bacteria into deep xylem where lack of moisture causes death)
woodSpecies.dishwasherVulnerability: High (Rapid swelling, differential shrinkage across annual rings, fiber checking)
woodSpecies.description: The gold standard for commercial butcher blocks and professional kitchen spoons. Hard sugar maple has dense, tightly packed closed grain with microscopic pores that resist deep liquid absorption. Under proper oil maintenance, it resists splitting and surface fraying.

woodSpecies.name: European Beech (Fagus sylvatica)
woodSpecies.dishwasherVulnerability: Very High (High tangential shrinkage ratio ~11.8%; warps and checks quickly)
woodSpecies.description: The most common European timber for classic culinary wooden spoons. Offers smooth machinability and good mechanical toughness. However, beech has one of the highest moisture shrinkage differentials of commercial hardwoods, making it particularly prone to warping and crack expansion if washed in a dishwasher.

woodSpecies.name: Moso Bamboo (Phyllostachys edulis)
woodSpecies.poreStructure: Vascular Bundles in Parenchyma Ground Tissue (Silica-Rich)
woodSpecies.naturalAntimicrobialProperties: Low-to-Moderate (High silica surface barrier, but zero innate bioactive compounds)
woodSpecies.dishwasherVulnerability: Extreme (Adhesive delamination; urea-formaldehyde or PVA glues hydrolyze under hot water)
woodSpecies.capillaryAbsorptionRate: Low along outer culm; High along exposed strip seams
woodSpecies.description: Not true timber, but laminated culm strips glued with food-contact adhesives. While naturally water-resistant and hard due to silica phytoliths, dishwasher heat (65°C+) and alkaline detergents hydrolyze the laminating resins, causing longitudinal separation, splintering, and harboring deep bacterial colonies along glue lines.

woodSpecies.name: Mediterranean Olive Wood (Olea europaea)
woodSpecies.poreStructure: Irregular Dense Grain with Interlocked Fibers
woodSpecies.naturalAntimicrobialProperties: High (Rich in natural oleuropein, hydroxytyrosol polyphenols, and hydrophobic natural resins)
woodSpecies.dishwasherVulnerability: Extreme (High density causes immense internal stress during rapid hot air drying, causing explosive shattering)
woodSpecies.capillaryAbsorptionRate: Very Low (Natural oily resins block fluid ingress)
woodSpecies.description: Extremely dense, heavy, and naturally hydrophobic. Natural polyphenols provide measurable bacteriostatic resistance against common microbes. However, its interlocked grain is hypersensitive to rapid thermal swings: putting an olive wood spoon in a dishwasher cycle causes severe internal stress fractures and deep splitting.

woodSpecies.name: Pine / Generic Softwood (Pinus strobus)
woodSpecies.poreStructure: Non-Porous / Open Tracheids (Large lumen volume, high void fraction)
woodSpecies.naturalAntimicrobialProperties: Low (High resin, but soft cell walls readily crush and shred under culinary friction)
woodSpecies.dishwasherVulnerability: Extreme (Fast fiber erosion, deep splintering, total leaching of natural resins)
woodSpecies.capillaryAbsorptionRate: Very High (Acts like a porous capillary sponge)
woodSpecies.description: Inexpensive, lightweight wood sometimes used in novelty or budget wooden spatulas. Highly unsuitable for serious cooking: low hardness allows spoons to dent and shred easily, creating deep fissures and fiber gouges that absorb large volumes of food juices and bacteria.

woodSpecies.name: Acacia Hardwood (Acacia mangium / nilotica)
woodSpecies.poreStructure: Medium Vessels with Abundant Tyloses Blocking Cavities
woodSpecies.naturalAntimicrobialProperties: High (Condensed tannins, catechin derivatives, and hydrophobic gums)
woodSpecies.dishwasherVulnerability: High (Surface dulling, extraction of protective tannins, surface fuzzing)
woodSpecies.description: Durable, moisture-tolerant tropical hardwood rich in natural protective tannins and tyloses (balloon-like outgrowths that naturally plug wood vascular vessels). Resists water absorption better than beech, but alkaline dishwashing detergents strip its protective surface resins.

exposureHistories.name: Gentle Handwash Only (Hot Water + Mild Soap + Air Dry)
exposureHistories.description: Cleaned by hand immediately after use with lukewarm-to-hot water (40–45°C), mild surfactant dish soap, non-abrasive sponge, and dried upright in an open dish rack. Wood fibers stay compact, micro-cracks remain sealed (< 35 µm).

exposureHistories.name: Occasional Dishwasher Exposure (1–5 Machine Cycles)
exposureHistories.description: Accidentally placed in the dishwasher a few times. Hot water (65°C) and alkaline sodium carbonate/metasilicate detergents have swelled surface fibers, causing the wood grain to 'raise' with a rough, fuzzy texture and opening early micro-fissures (50–100 µm).

exposureHistories.name: Frequent Dishwasher Exposure (10–25 Machine Cycles)
exposureHistories.description: Subjected to regular dishwasher wash cycles and heated dry (75°C). The alternating water saturation and intense hot air baking strips natural hemicellulose and lignin binders. Surface is faded grey/white, rough to the touch, with visible cracks (150–350 µm) penetrating deep into the handle and bowl.

exposureHistories.name: Chronic Dishwasher Exposure (50+ Machine Cycles)
exposureHistories.description: Severely degraded utensil. Deep structural fissures (> 500–1000 µm) run along the grain. The wood is brittle, splintered, and hyper-porous. In bamboo, glue lines have separated into hollow crevices. Microbial decontamination is scientifically impossible without shaving or discarding.

conditioningStatuses.name: Well-Maintained: USP Food-Grade Mineral Oil + Beeswax Seal
conditioningStatuses.rancidityRisk: Zero (Saturated alkane hydrocarbons do not oxidize or turn rancid)
conditioningStatuses.description: Treated monthly with pure USP liquid paraffin (food-grade mineral oil) and sealed with beeswax. Saturated hydrocarbons penetrate deep into wood tracheids and vessels, filling internal air cavities and repelling water, juices, and bacterial migration.

conditioningStatuses.name: Infrequent Maintenance: Conditioned 1–2x per Year
conditioningStatuses.description: Oil has partially washed out from daily washing. The surface is dry to the touch, and capillary suction is moderately active, though deep pores retain residual hydrophobic protection.

conditioningStatuses.name: Unconditioned: Raw, Dry & Parched Wood
conditioningStatuses.description: Raw, unprotected wood fibers. When in contact with aqueous foods, strong capillary capillary action (suction pressure up to 2.5 MPa in dry cell walls) sucks contaminated juices, fats, and bacteria deep into the core within seconds.

conditioningStatuses.name: Improperly Conditioned: Vegetable / Olive / Canola Oil
conditioningStatuses.rancidityRisk: Extreme (Polyunsaturated fats undergo lipid peroxidation → malondialdehyde & hexanal)
conditioningStatuses.description: Culinary oils containing polyunsaturated fatty acids (linoleic, oleic) oxidize upon exposure to light and ambient oxygen. Forms a sticky, gummy, yellowish varnish that emits a rancid odor, fails to repel moisture properly, and acts as a biological nutrient substrate for bacterial growth.

foodContactMatrices.name: Raw Chicken / Turkey / Pork Juices
foodContactMatrices.description: High moisture, high protein liquid containing dense pathogenic bacteria. Capillary suction draws viable Salmonella deep into microscopic wood vessel lumens where standard brief surface rinsing cannot reach.

foodContactMatrices.name: Raw Ground Beef / Meat Juices
foodContactMatrices.description: Myoglobin-rich fluid carrying enteric bacteria and Staphylococci. Enters cracks and binds to cellulose fibrils, creating a resilient biofilm base.

foodContactMatrices.name: Simmering Acidic Tomato Stew / Chili (95°C, pH 3.8)
foodContactMatrices.targetPathogens: Heat-killed vegetative cells; surviving spore-formers (Bacillus cereus)
foodContactMatrices.crossContaminationHazard: Low for live pathogens (thermal kill > 74°C), High for wood degradation & chemical leeching
foodContactMatrices.description: Sustained high cooking temperatures pasteurize surface vegetative bacteria, but hot acid hydrolyzes wood hemicellulose and leaches bound oils into the sauce.

foodContactMatrices.name: Cold Salad Greens / Fruit / Baby Food Prep (Cold Service)
foodContactMatrices.crossContaminationHazard: Critical Cross-Contamination Vector (Zero Kill Step before consumption)
foodContactMatrices.description: Ready-to-eat foods that undergo no further heating. If a wooden spoon previously used for raw poultry or washed ineffectively touches this food, active bacteria in surface cracks transfer directly to the consumer.

foodContactMatrices.name: High-Fat Cream Curry / Coconut Gravy / Bolognese
foodContactMatrices.crossContaminationHazard: High (Lipids seal moisture inside pores, insulating bacteria from detergents)
foodContactMatrices.description: Lipids penetrate deeply into porous wood cracks. Standard detergent washing without scalding water fails to saponify and remove deep fats, leaving food reserves for bacterial biofilm.

dryingEnvironments.name: Open-Air Vertical Dish Rack (Ventilated, RH < 50%)
dryingEnvironments.description: Optimal post-wash hygiene. Air circulation evaporates surface moisture within 90 minutes. Rapid surface water activity reduction (Aw < 0.65) halts bacterial division and initiates natural desiccation.

dryingEnvironments.name: Crowded Ceramic Utensil Crock (Handles Down, Heads Touching)
dryingEnvironments.description: Spoons shoved together in an unventilated ceramic crock while damp. Trapped moisture at the bottom of the jar creates a dark, humid micro-climate (RH > 85%) where bacteria multiply exponentially for 6 to 12 hours.

dryingEnvironments.name: Enclosed Dark Drawer / Cupboard (Stored Damp)
dryingEnvironments.description: Stored damp in a dark enclosed drawer. Persistent moisture and room temperature allow bacterial biofilms to consolidate and fungal mold spores (Aspergillus, Penicillium) to germinate inside wood cracks.

pathogens.name: Salmonella enterica (Non-Typhoidal)
pathogens.woodPorePersistenceDays: Up to 28 days (Enters viable but non-culturable VBNC state in dry wood)

pathogens.name: Staphylococcus aureus & Heat-Stable Enterotoxins
pathogens.woodPorePersistenceDays: Up to 60 days (High osmotic and salt tolerance)
pathogens.thermalDValue: Bacteria killed at 70°C, but Enterotoxin A resists boiling at 100°C for 30+ min
pathogens.clinicalHazard: Rapid-onset projectile vomiting and severe cramps within 1–6 hours

pathogens.name: Escherichia coli (Pathogenic EHEC / STEC)
pathogens.woodPorePersistenceDays: Up to 21 days in moist fissures
pathogens.clinicalHazard: Bloody diarrhea, Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (HUS), acute renal failure

pathogens.name: Listeria monocytogenes
pathogens.woodPorePersistenceDays: Up to 90 days (Forms dense extracellular polysaccharide EPS biofilms)
pathogens.clinicalHazard: Meningitis, sepsis, 20–30% mortality in immunocompromised and pregnant women

pathogens.name: Fungal Wood Rot & Mold (Aspergillus / Cladosporium)
pathogens.infectiousDose: Inhalation of mycotoxins & ingestion of decomposed fibers
pathogens.woodPorePersistenceDays: Indefinite (Spore dormant for years in unsealed wood crevices)
pathogens.clinicalHazard: Allergic reactions, fungal mycotoxins, wood decay and off-flavors
